archived.description: Hidden from ordinary listings, without stopping execution or deleting history.

by.description: who archived it — kept as history when that entity is deleted

via.description: the instrument it was written through — the session or client the write came in on

ask.description: the model was asked here, from the prefix ending at `through`; what the provider keeps about it rides in that provider's own comp beside this one

through.description: the last entry of the prefix it was asked with

attempt.description: Provider request lifecycle. Unfinished dispatched attempts are ambiguous on restart, never automatically replayed.

attention.description: a line that wants to be read before the next ask

brief.description: the session’s own account of itself, written at the end and quoted in the next one

cancel.description: a line that withdraws an earlier one

checkpoint.description: everything through this entry is settled: a compaction boundary

claim.description: a session’s lock on the entity carrying it

session.description: the session holding it — when that session’s entity dies the lock goes and the entity lives

at.description: when it was taken — stamped when the lock is new

conflict.description: two sessions wanted one thing: written after the refusal, never by a client

loser.description: the session whose write was refused

holder.description: the session that already held the lock

dispatch.description: durable child pool admission; queued intent survives daemon restart

entry.description: one line of a transcript; the comp beside it says what kind

seq.description: Positive integer position; omit on append to allocate atomically. Explicit fractional or occupied positions are refused.

fork.description: this session continues another transcript from one of its entries

from.description: the entry this fork continues from: the parent's entries up to it are this transcript's prefix

imported.description: a line that came from somewhere else — which transcript, and which line of it

notice.description: passive transcript context, included in the next ask without requesting one

task.description: the task that prompted this notice

reasoning.description: a line the model thought rather than said

resume.description: set aside by an actor to come back to, with its place in the stack

session.description: a transcript something reacts to. Identity only: what it is doing is read off its entries (`status`), where it runs is @yaks/process `process`, and what it was asked for is the `using` on its first entry

id.description: the runner’s own name for it

actor.description: who it speaks as — the identity that survives a /clear, where `created.by` is the run

operator.description: true when a person is driving this transcript rather than an agent

standing.description: a session that stays: named here rather than ended when its work is done

status.description: what the newest entry says: pending awaits the model, running awaits an answer, settled has nothing to do

spawned.description: a child session delegated by a parent; fork independently selects an inherited prefix

stop.description: a mark in the transcript: the daemon performs nothing after it

using.description: provider, model and effort: on an input it sets or switches them, on an ask it records what was served

provider.description: the provider asked — kept as history when that entity is deleted, so a past ask still says what answered it

model.description: the model asked — kept as history when that entity is deleted, so a past ask still says what answered it

instructions.description: system instructions in force for this transcript

claim_take.title: Claim it
claim_take.description: Take the lock on an entity for a session, so nobody else picks it up. A lease, not a patch: writing one over another session’s lock fails the whole batch — release first. The same session re-claiming is a no-op refresh.

target.description: the entity to lock — any entity at all

session.description: the session holding it (default: whoever is asking)

claim_release.title: Let it go
claim_release.description: Drop the lock on an entity. Unguarded on purpose: letting go is how a lock is handed over, and a dead session’s locks are freed by whoever notices.

target.description: the entity to lock — any entity at all

session_context.title: What this session was in the middle of
session_context.description: Start of a transcript: find or mint the session entity for a harness’s session id, and answer what it was in the middle of — what it holds a claim on, and the last thing the actor behind it said about itself. The harness injects the prose; nothing here fails loudly.

session.description: the harness's own name for the transcript

hook.description: a harness lifecycle payload as JSON — `-` reads it from stdin, which is how a hook hands its event over

actor.description: who it speaks as — the identity that survives a /clear

session_wrap.title: End of a transcript
session_wrap.description: End of a transcript: record the session’s own account of itself, and release every lock it still holds. A session that was never reified wraps to nothing.

session.description: the harness's own name for the transcript

hook.description: a harness lifecycle payload as JSON — `-` reads it from stdin, which is how a hook hands its event over

brief.description: what this session did, in its own words

session_brief.title: Say what happened
session_brief.description: Write the session’s own account of itself — the brief the next session by the same actor is handed. Replaces whatever it said before.

session.description: the harness's own name for the transcript

hook.description: a harness lifecycle payload as JSON — `-` reads it from stdin, which is how a hook hands its event over

hooks_install.title: Wire the injection loop
hooks_install.description: Write this package’s lifecycle entries into a harness settings file, so every session starts by reading its context back and ends by wrapping. Replaces an earlier install and leaves every other entry alone. Runs on the box the tool runs on.

yak.description: how the yak command is spelled on this box
